text: Same car. Same price.
But Doug pay ten thousand dollars more.
What the difference?
One number.
This is called credit score.
Score go from three hundred to eight fifty.
Higher is better.
Credit score is like report card. But for money.
Three big companies keep this report. Equifax. Experian. TransUnion.
When Doug want loan, bank look at this number.
Bank rent you money. Interest is the rent.
High number. Bank trust you. Lower interest.
Low number. Bank scared. Higher interest.
Friend score: seven ninety. Average interest: six percent.
Doug score: five fifty. Average interest: nineteen percent.
Car cost twenty-five thousand. Five years.
Every month, friend pay four eighty-seven. Doug pay six fifty-four.
Friend pay four thousand in interest.
Doug pay fourteen thousand.
Ten thousand dollars. For one number.
Doug poor.
So why Doug score so low?
Doug pay bill late.
Doug use all his credit card.
Doug open five cards in one month.
Bank see this. Bank see risk.
Doug angry.
In real life, average used car loan is about nineteen percent for low score.
About six percent for high score.
Same car. Different number. Different price.
What is your credit score? Tell Doug.
